description: Use this when a signed-in operator asks whether a monitored domain is ready for the next DMARC step. Read the DMARC enforcement-readiness verdict for ONE domain the caller's account monitors, computed from its aggregate (RUA) report window. Requires an API token. Returns whether the domain is ready to step its policy up, the blockers that say why it is not, the window the verdict rests on, and next_record — the validated record for the next step, generated by the engine and null while blocked. THAT NULL IS AN ANSWER: relay the blockers and never compose a stronger record to fill the gap. Present a returned record verbatim; a human must approve it before it is published. Use this before proposing enforcement — a scan can show a domain's current policy, but only this evidence window can say whether tightening it would start rejecting real mail.

domain.description: One of the token account's VERIFIED monitored domains, e.g. example.com. Any other name — another account's, or one nobody monitors — is refused as not found; ownership is never disclosed.
